intro: The authoring harnesses. Not product — they exist to decide numbers by looking at things side by side: how many discrete poses, what to do with the spring's tail, how an unvalidated pair looks. What gets decided here is what ends up as the library's default.

iconImport.desdeEditor: Loaded {{nombre}} from the geometry editor, with its original choreography. Previewed below.
iconImport.instrucciones: Paste the JSON you copied from "Export JSON" in the detail panel. It previews with the same [iconDef] the rest of the playground uses.

errores.jsonInvalido: Invalid JSON — check your commas and braces.
errores.shapesInvalidas: "shapes" must have at least one figure, and each one needs a "tag".

morphPicker.expectativa: The core pairs subpaths by proximity — if two icons share nothing in common, there's no good geometric match to find. When that happens, the engine detects it on its own and uses a fade (opacity, no points to interpolate) instead of forcing a deformation that would look worse. Legs marked fade in the chain are those cases — that's not an error, it's the fallback working.
morphPicker.fundidoTooltip: Fallback to fade: no valid geometric match.
morphPicker.leyendaFundido: Amber: no valid geometric morph is available, so glyphFlow falls back to a fade.
morphPicker.vacioLienzo: Choose at least 2 icons to build a sequence.

morphBench.intro: One pair at a time, 4 variants side by side. The spring only decides the timing: zero animation loop — the keyframes are computed once and the browser interpolates them.

controles.resolucionNota: res is the sampling resolution: how many points each subpath is resampled to before the two shapes are paired up. It samples the OUTLINE, not time — it changes how faithfully the curve is followed, never how many frames play.

avisos.pasos:
More steps track the path more closely, at the cost of a bigger keyframe array — fidelity against payload.

Technical details

Adaptive is the real default: it doesn't hand out an even count across all 1767 icons, only the pairs that actually rotate get more. Compare it against 20 steps on bell → bell-ring (should look identical) and against 10 on circle → square (fewer steps, same fidelity, because it barely rotates).
avisos.cola: The tail only shows up on the way back: turn on Loop and watch it land. "No reverse" doesn't come back — it restarts from the origin every cycle.
avisos.sobrepaso:
An underdamped spring overshoots the target and comes back.

Technical details

That used to just stretch the clock: the icon would arrive and sit still. Now the overshoot poses render by default — the comparison that matters is snappy, undrawn (sobrepaso: false) against snappy. bouncy is clamped: extrapolating further would push it off the canvas and the SVG would clip it.
avisos.vuelta: Hover in, then pull out — that's the real case (reverseOnLeave). reverse() walks the offsets in mirror and lands abruptly; Round trip carries its own spring on each leg and doesn't need you to pull out.

envoltorio.descripcion: The thin wrapper. A single [icon]: changing it triggers the morph from the previous value. The first render paints static — there's nowhere to transition from.
envoltorio.avisoChico: Underdamped springs overshoot the target and come back. Hit "next" with bouncy and watch the overshoot — that's what didn't used to render.

comparacion.descripcion: Same pair, two engines. Baked precomputes ~20 poses and WAAPI interpolates linearly between them. Live recomputes the exact position every frame — the difference shows most on pairs with real rotation.

tabla.leyenda:
keyframes — interpolated poses.

weight — size of the keyframe array in memory (not bundle weight — computed in your browser when the morph runs, ships with nothing).

duration — how long one leg of the morph lasts.

last leg — share of that duration spent on the final step. Higher means it crawls to a stop.

deviation — how far the interpolation strays from the real path. The metric behind Adaptive.
